verdict.detail: Move the money from Pinckert to Banks, and use the freed cash to upgrade the keeper as well. This reverses the standing Pinckert plan. The offer sitting on Pinckert is the second-highest premium over market value this ledger has ever priced on a board listing, and we are the only bidder on it. Banks is the same kind of asset — a defender with two full starts and a marginally better average — listed at exactly market value with nobody bidding, and his auction resolves later. The two cannot both be held: the squad is at eleven, so each buy permits exactly one sale, and holding both would leave the balance negative at matchday start, which scores zero for the whole matchday. So it is one or the other, and Banks is better, cheaper and later. Withdrawing Pinckert also frees enough to bid on Neuer, which is a straight keeper swap that leaves the formation untouched. Together the two trades lift the fielded eleven by a meaningful margin at essentially no net cash cost. The action is time-boxed: if the Pinckert offer is left standing it wins this afternoon, consumes the only usable unwind, and kills both other trades.
